claim: A system is diagnosable when every fault trace is followed, within finite delay, by observations that only fault states can produce. It is tested on the model, off-line, with a diagnoser (exponential) or a twin plant (quadratic).
schema_part: S0 model of the task (design-time check)
agent_test: Define for each task a set of candidate hypotheses and the observations the agent can obtain; check by script whether any two hypotheses give identical outputs on every available probe.

claim: Non-diagnosability has one structural cause: two different faults (or a fault and nominal) give the same observations forever. Loops of uncertain states are the witness. Example: a stuck-open valve and a normally open valve with only a flow sensor.
agent_test: Build tasks with two causes that no allowed probe separates; measure whether the agent says it cannot tell or picks one.

claim: Indicator events matter: some faults show only after a command. I-diagnosability asks for detection only after the indicator event, so a system can look undiagnosable because nobody triggered the test.
agent_test: Compare an agent allowed to trigger the relevant action versus one that only watches, at equal tokens.

claim: Complexity: strong diagnosability of a monolithic automaton is quadratic and optimal under standard conjectures; weak diagnosability, modular systems and succinct systems are hard (PSPACE or worse). Minimum-sensor design is NP-complete (clique and colouring reductions).
agent_test: Do not give the agent an exact checker for big systems; use a cheap heuristic (count of hypothesis pairs still unseparated) and compare with exact answers on small cases.

claim: SAT encodings of the twin plant find non-diagnosability witnesses in systems with 160 to 200 components where explicit twin plants (6^(2C) states) cannot be built.
agent_test: If the agent must check separability on large hypothesis sets, test a SAT or solver tool call against a pure-text check at equal tokens.

claim: Diagnosability is a property of a belief state and a probe set, not of the system alone. It can hold at the start and fail after a repair or fault. When it fails, one action plan (PSPACE-complete) can restore it; sensor sets can also be switched on and off dynamically (polynomial check).
schema_part: S (re-check separability when beliefs change) / O (probe selection)
agent_test: After each new observation, have the agent list which remaining hypothesis pairs are still inseparable; compare with a fixed plan.

claim: Active test selection by expected information gain (entropy of the split of remaining candidates) lifts LLM diagnosis and question-asking over letting the LLM pick questions freely. UoT GPT-4 closed-set success 71.2/37.5/97.0/88.0/67.3 vs direct 50.5/30.5/91.3/72.3/43.7; BED-LLM 20 Questions +37.4 points; ACTMED halves tests with equal accuracy.
agent_test: Add an operator: ask the probe that most evenly splits the live hypotheses; compare with free-form probing at matched tokens on closed-set fault tasks.

claim: Open-set gains are smaller and absolute scores low: when the candidate list is not given, UoT gain over direct prompting shrinks (GPT-4 DX 49.1 vs 44.2; Common 55.3 vs 48.6).
agent_test: Run the same probe operator with and without a supplied candidate list.

claim: Information-gain scaffolds keep their gain at matched cost in UoT (9.2k tokens: 54.4/92.5/66.0 vs Adapted-ToT 4.5k: 33.8/85.1/60.3), and MAI-DxO reached 80% at lower dollar cost than plain o3 (70% less). But coding-agent harnesses on Cloud-OpsBench bought process quality with 2 to 4 times the tokens. Note UoT used twice the tokens of its ToT comparator, so the match is not exact. New: AR-BED measured BED-LLM at 61.1x the per-game time of a trained policy (d08); still no equal-token comparison against best-of-N found.
agent_test: Always report accuracy at fixed token budget; include a plain-prompt arm given the same extra tokens (best-of-N or longer CoT).

claim: LLMs that pick their own tests keep choosing the same globally useful test for every case and ask redundant questions; they do not adapt to current uncertainty. A sequential-BED search summary also says LLMs do not consistently beat random experiments (not opened). New: in 2026 models (Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.1 and four others) 24.1% of 6,596 probes separated truth from an alternative vs 19.2% at random (d03).
schema_part: O (test selection) / G (do not trust own test choice)
agent_test: Log how often the chosen probe has zero expected split on the live set (redundant probe rate).

claim: Holding the belief only in the prompt context fails; an explicit hypothesis set with filtering, a causal graph or a state machine works. BED-LLM GPT-4o Animals: in-context beliefs 25 vs explicit 93 (prompt-only 45). GoS medical ablation Match: no causal graph 18.12, no state machine 12.32. Context graphs account for 94% of post-switch gain. New: BED-LLM ablation, Qwen2.5-72B Animals: ICL Beliefs 46, Implicit Max 61, Split 87, BED-LLM 95 (d11), so the scored split step carries most of the gain.
agent_test: Compare a ledger of live hypotheses with support and refute marks versus free-text history at equal tokens.

claim: Standard chain, tree and graph prompting show four failures in abduction: evidence fabrication (22.22% in pooled baselines), context drift (41.32%), early stopping (63.89%), failed backtracking. A state machine plus causal graph cut the first three (0, 9.70, 18.75) but backtracking failures stayed at 30.90%.
agent_test: Tag each agent failure by these four types on a fault-diagnosis set; check whether the ledger removes fabrication.

claim: A correct final answer does not mean a grounded diagnosis. GPT-5 named the right root cause without evidence closure in 33.1% (OnlineBoutique) and 29.4% (TrainTicket) of Cloud-OpsBench cases; PAVE found 76.0% name a correct service but only 61.5% ground it in a verified path, and the exact root-cause set is recovered 20.7%. New: in a gene-network fault task all 7 LLMs fixed more than they diagnosed (Opus 4.6 1.00 vs 0.55) (d01).
agent_test: Score answer and evidence path separately; count right-for-wrong-reason answers.

claim: Having the right cause in the candidate pool does not mean choosing it. Pool-minus-final gap: SIA 10.0, THK-int 11.9, ReAct 17.5, ToT 22.5. The gap cannot separate missing evidence from selection error, which is exactly what a diagnosability check would split. New: with a known isolability matrix only 7 of 60 cases were structurally non-diagnosable, diagnosis 0.12 there vs 0.30 elsewhere, so selection and evidence-use error dominates in that domain (d02).
agent_test: Report potential (oracle over pool) and final separately; use a separability check to label each miss as not-diagnosable-with-this-evidence or selection error.

claim: A hypothesis-keeping investigator that asks a counterfactual question separating its top two explanations beat baselines: SIA final 79.2 [72.7,83.7] vs BAS 67.3, ReAct 69.0, ToT 61.5, THK-int 72.8, Ask-5 72.3 (100 cases). Gain holds on two other backbones (+6.2, +7.7). Ablation: removing structured investigation costs 6.4, counterfactual critique 5.2. Same-authors, one benchmark.
agent_test: Implement: ask the question that separates the top two hypotheses; test at equal tokens vs Ask-5.

claim: Small, weak evidence: a plausible wrong user conjecture lowered SIA from 80.0 to 76.0 and was selected in 2 of 10 pairs.
agent_test: Run a larger paired stress test (at least 100 pairs) before any claim.

claim: LLMs collapse to the most probable single fault and miss valid multi-fault candidates: in Circuit 1 Scenario 2 only 1 of 13 models named the double fault. Overall hit rates 79.5% (Gemini 2.5 Flash) down to 0%; hallucination 15.4% to 94.9%.
agent_test: Test an operator that forces minimal-candidate-set enumeration (hitting sets) before ranking; score on multi-fault cases.

claim: LLM performance on structural diagnosis steps falls as the combinatorics grow. o3-mini conflicts F1 0.917, diagnoses F1 0.784; incidence matrix is easy (o1, o3-mini F1 1.00; 4o-mini 0.47). Plank: on the hardest circuit all small models below 0.60, large above 1.70.
schema_part: G (do not trust unaided enumeration beyond small sizes) / tools
agent_test: Compute hitting sets by code and compare with the model's own enumeration as hypothesis count rises (to about 150).

claim: Memorised textbook examples inflate scores: Phi-2 scored 1.05 on powertrain but 0.08 to 0.67 elsewhere; the authors flag the standard two-bulb circuit as possibly memorised. Sztyber-Betley released solutions after model release to control this; gpt-4o and 4o-mini were near zero on unseen cases without code.
agent_test: Use novel generated systems, not literature circuits, and keep held-out sets private.

claim: Some faults cannot be told apart from the available telemetry. GPT-5 scored JRA 0.00 on hard TrainTicket performance faults; resource saturation from injection vs a code defect cannot be separated without source. Removing source access hurts all models and raises implausible causes.
schema_part: O (get a different probe) / G (say cannot tell)
agent_test: Include tasks provably non-diagnosable from the given evidence; reward asking for more evidence over a guess.

claim: LLMs propose confirming rather than falsifying tests. Eleven LLMs on rule discovery: counterexample prompting lifts the average rule-discovery rate from 42% to 56%. Disjunctive-bias reports exist only as a search summary.
agent_test: Add an explicit step: name a probe that would break the leading hypothesis; compare rule-discovery at equal tokens.

claim: Being good at the fully specified problem does not predict being good at asking the one question that makes it solvable. QuestBench: Logic-Q and Planning-Q all models under 50%; GSM-Q strong models above 80%.
agent_test: Test the agent on underspecified tasks with exactly one missing variable; measure question accuracy separately from solve accuracy.

claim: Entropy-based query selection needs far fewer oracle queries than split-in-half or random in classic interactive debugging (more than 50% fewer; 33,000-axiom ontology resolved with about 5 queries in 190 s), and DynamicHS beats HS-Tree in 96% of sessions (median saving 52%). Minimum possible is log2(n).
agent_test: Use log2(n) as a lower bound on probes; report probes used versus bound.

claim: Fault isolability can be stated structurally: fault f is isolable from f' if some fault-MSO set contains f but not f'. Sensor placement can be solved by Dulmage-Mendelsohn decomposition given a per-variable cost; FDI and DX communities developed the idea separately.
agent_test: Generate benchmark systems with a known isolability matrix, so ground truth for which pairs are separable is exact.

claim: Task success does not imply cause identification in 2026 models: every one of 7 LLMs scored higher on rescue than diagnosis (Opus 4.6 1.00 vs 0.55; GPT-5.1 0.40 vs 0.15); diagnosis varied about 7x across models while outcome prediction varied 1.4x.
schema_part: G (do not accept a working fix as a diagnosis)
agent_test: Score cause and outcome separately on a held-out fault set with known cause.

claim: True structural non-diagnosability was rare in one fault benchmark with a known isolability matrix: 7 of 60 organisms. Diagnosis was 0.31, 0.30, 0.12 for unambiguous, resolvable and structural classes. Most error is selection and evidence use.
agent_test: Build 30 cases with a computed isolability table; log how many wrong answers fall in non-separable pairs.

claim: Agents barely prefer separating probes: 24.1% vs 19.2% at random over 6,596 experiments, while 91% of sessions still met a discriminating result and diagnosis there was 0.30. Pairing probes in both directions on the true cause: 0.71 vs 0.04.
agent_test: Count probes that split the live hypotheses; compare scaffolded vs free choice at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs do not reliably call a result uninformative: with the two causes' predictions within noise, accuracy was 0.30 to 0.53 and models usually picked the numerically closer prediction. When predictions are given, accuracy is 0.88 to 1.00; when they must be derived, 0.51 to 0.74.
schema_part: S (ledger of per-hypothesis predictions); abstain verdict
agent_test: Give the agent pairs whose predictions overlap; score 'cannot tell' answers against an isolability table.

claim: The separability verdict is better made by code than by the LLM: a graph-search verifier gave 100% precision across three LLMs, while the LLM only labelled device roles and recall tracked LLM quality. This is observability, not pairwise isolability.
agent_test: Compare an LLM-only 'can these be told apart' verdict against a script on 100 small models.

claim: Information-gain gains are shown only for non-reasoning or small models. Reasoning at inference lowered solve rate in a small model (d08); ASIG gain fell from 7B to 14B (d10); BED-LLM tested no reasoning questioner (d12). No test with a 2026 frontier reasoning model as the questioner was found.
agent_test: Run the split-probe operator on top of a frontier reasoning model vs the same model alone at equal tokens.

claim: The Cloud-OpsBench scoring gives credit for a committed root cause and has no abstain option; 22% of audited right-answer-weak-process cases ended with ambiguous observations that did not rule out rival faults. Whether abstaining improves calibrated accuracy is untested.
schema_part: G (abstain or probe when not separable)
agent_test: Add an abstain option with a cost; measure accuracy on answered cases vs coverage.

claim: No paper found tests whether an LLM can decide diagnosability (two faults, no allowed probe separates them) from a system model. Closest: d04 (uninformative result), d15 (observability by code).
agent_test: Build the direct test: small models with known isolability matrices; ask the LLM which pairs are inseparable.
